_note: Synthetic probe suite for the lexical-fingerprint gap analysis (METHODOLOGY.md Part X). Each probe is a 100-250 word text in ISDS-report register, authored to isolate a specific behaviour of the deterministic keyword scorer (src/classify.py::keyword_score against fingerprint.yaml). 'expected_band' is the band the OPERATOR'S THEME DEFINITION implies the item deserves; it is NOT a claim about what the current instrument scores. Probes whose current score contradicts expected_band are the evidence. Bands: HIGH >=70, MEDIUM 40-69, LOW <40. Digest threshold = 40. These are synthetic texts; see the red-team section of analytics/fingerprint-gap-report.md for the limits of synthetic validation.

probes.text: Nordica Biologics AS v. Republic of Costa Verde. The Icelandic claimant asserts that its confidential clinical trial data and pharmaceutical trade secrets, submitted to the national medicines agency to obtain marketing approval, constitute a covered investment under the Iceland-Costa Verde BIT. In 2025 the agency approved a domestic generic manufacturer by relying on the originator's undisclosed test or other data, a step the claimant characterises as an unfair commercial use contrary to the host state's regulatory data protection regime and TRIPS Article 39. The claimant frames the agency measure, not any court ruling, as the challenged administrative measure. Costa Verde contests jurisdiction, disputing the definition of investor and arguing the data package never amounted to treaty protection-eligible property. It further pleads abuse of process, alleging the claimant engineered treaty protection through a late corporate restructuring after the dispute was reasonably foreseeable. The tribunal must decide whether regulatory data rights qualify as an investment and whether the administrative disclosure breached the minimum standard of treatment.
probes.rationale: Einarsson shape with DENSE exact vocabulary: Ring 1 (trade secret + clinical trial data + covered investment + regulatory data protection + unfair commercial use + TRIPS 39) intersects Ring 3 (definition of investor + abuse of process + corporate restructuring + reasonably foreseeable + treaty protection). Two rings present -> should be HIGH. Tests that the reweighted Ring 1 works when reporting happens to use the exact terms.

probes.text: Meridian Therapeutics v. Republic of Andalor. The claimant contends that the clinical trial data it generated to secure marketing authorisation for its biologic is proprietary commercial information and a trade secret amounting to an investment. It alleges that the national drug regulator, by an administrative decision, permitted a competitor to rely on that data to obtain its own approval, and separately published portions of the dossier in a transparency register. The claimant says this measure destroyed the value of years of proprietary research, breached the fair and equitable treatment standard, and was arbitrary and unreasonable. No court proceeding is at issue anywhere; the claim targets the regulator's conduct directly through investor-state arbitration under the applicable BIT. Andalor responds that the alleged rights are ordinary regulatory permissions, not property, and that the claimant holds no protected asset. The parties dispute whether confidential data submitted to a regulator can be an asset capable of expropriation.
probes.rationale: The CORE false-negative shape. On-theme trade-secret/clinical-data investment claim against a purely administrative measure, FET pleaded in the phrasing real awards use ('fair and equitable treatment', not the seed's 'minimum standard of treatment'; 'arbitrary and unreasonable', not 'arbitrary or discriminatory'). Ring 1 lands trade secret (9) + clinical trial data (8) = 17, just under STRONG_SUBTOTAL; Ring 2 and Ring 3 lexicon does not fire at all. Should be MEDIUM; the instrument scores 33 (LOW). Deliberately avoids the words 'administrative measure' and 'domestic court' so the miss is not masked by an incidental (or negated) phrase hit.

probes.text: Helvetia Vaccines SA v. Republic of Sargasso. A Swiss originator alleges that Sargasso's health ministry granted an abbreviated approval to a generic rival by relying on the claimant's undisclosed test or other data, and that ministry officials disclosed elements of its clinical trial data to third parties. The claimant asserts these trade secrets are a covered investment and that the ministry's administrative measures constituted an unfair commercial use in violation of the minimum standard of treatment. It does not challenge any judicial ruling; the entire claim rests on regulatory conduct. Sargasso disputes that regulatory submissions can be an investment and reserves its jurisdictional objections on the definition of investor.
probes.rationale: Einarsson shape with DENSE Ring 1 (undisclosed test or other data + clinical trial data + trade secret + covered investment + unfair commercial use ~= 32) and a weak Ring 2/Ring 3 tie ('minimum standard of treatment' 6, 'definition of investor' 5, both sub-floor). Single strong Ring 1 + weak second ring -> MEDIUM. Tests the reweight succeeding when Ring 1 density is high even without a second present ring.

probes.text: Award summary. A pharmaceutical claimant asserted that its trade secret formulations and clinical trial data, filed with the national regulator to obtain approval, were an investment protected by the treaty. The tribunal disagreed. It held that the data was not an investment and that lodging a dossier with an administrative measure created no protected asset, echoing the outer limit drawn in earlier regulatory-rights cases. The measure complained of was the agency's approval of a rival product, a purely administrative act; no court was involved. Because the claimant was found not to be an investor with a qualifying investment, the tribunal declined jurisdiction and never reached the merits of the alleged unfair use of the dossier.
probes.rationale: The Apotex / Hela Schwarz negative-space shape: a decided REJECTION of trade-secret/clinical-data-as-investment against an administrative measure. The watcher wants these outer-limit rulings, but Ring 1 has no negation-aware phrasing and the report avoids 'covered investment' / 'definition of investor'. Ring 1 = trade secret (9) + clinical trial data (8) = 17, Ring 2/3 = 0. Should be MEDIUM; scores LOW. Also carries 'administrative measure' for the proposed Ring 2 cluster to catch.

probes.text: A foreign investor in the biosimilars sector has commenced treaty arbitration against the host state. The investor claims that the medicines regulator unlawfully relied on, and partially disclosed, its confidential business information and clinical data package when approving three competing products. The investor treats this proprietary regulatory data as the core of its protected investment and says the marketing-approval decisions, an administrative measure rather than a judicial one, expropriated it and denied fair and equitable treatment. The host state disputes that a data package submitted for approval is an asset it can be said to have taken, and challenges whether the investor even qualifies under the treaty. The tribunal will hear the regulator's administrative measures alone; no court judgment is challenged.
probes.rationale: Register-level brittleness probe. Squarely on-theme (pharmaceutical regulatory data as covered investment, administrative measure, jurisdiction contested) but written in the vocabulary real journalism/secondary reporting uses: 'confidential business information', 'clinical data', 'regulatory data', 'data package', 'marketing-approval', 'fair and equitable treatment'. NONE are exact fingerprint phrases. Ring 1 ~= 0 under current weights. Should be HIGH; scores ~0. Isolates the limit of a keyword instrument.

probes.text: A European originator initiates treaty arbitration against the host state over its 2026 pharmaceutical data regime. The claimant says the reforms hollowed out the promised six-year data exclusivity and the regulatory data protection it relied upon when it submitted its dossier for marketing approval, allowing domestic firms to obtain approvals on the strength of the originator's undisclosed test or other data. The claimant frames the data exclusivity entitlement as a covered investment and the regulatory reform as an administrative measure amounting to an unfair commercial use under TRIPS Article 39. It stresses that no court decision is challenged, only the drug administration's regulatory conduct. The respondent contests whether a data-protection expectancy can be an investment at all.
probes.rationale: China-regime shape, dense exact vocabulary, never says patent/trademark: data exclusivity + regulatory data protection + undisclosed test or other data + covered investment + unfair commercial use + TRIPS 39. Ring 1 alone should reach ~28 -> MEDIUM. Tests that the data-exclusivity vocabulary added in the July 2026 reweight actually clears the threshold.

probes.text: Reports indicate a Japanese pharmaceutical group is preparing an investment claim over the host state's revised marketing-approval pathway. The company argues that accelerated approvals for generic competitors unlawfully leveraged its regulatory data and eroded the exclusivity it was promised, undermining an investment worth hundreds of millions. The grievance centres on the national medical products administration's administrative decisions, not on any litigation in the courts. The company describes the loss of its data protection as a form of creeping expropriation and a denial of fair treatment, and says it will proceed to investor-state arbitration under the relevant bilateral investment treaty.
probes.rationale: China-regime shape in LOOSE vocabulary: 'regulatory data' (not 'regulatory data protection'), 'exclusivity' (not 'data exclusivity'), 'data protection' (not a phrase), 'marketing-approval', 'creeping expropriation', 'denial of fair treatment'. On-theme but Ring 1 ~= 0. Should be MEDIUM; scores near 0. Second register-brittleness false negative, on the China front specifically.

probes.text: A Swiss vaccine developer files for arbitration under the host state's bilateral investment treaty. It asserts that its clinical trial data and the data exclusivity granted on marketing approval are a covered investment, and that the national medical products administration breached protections when it approved biosimilars relying on the developer's regulatory data protection dossier, an unfair commercial use under TRIPS Article 39. The state raises jurisdictional objections: it disputes the definition of investor, alleges treaty shopping through a holding company, and says the dispute was reasonably foreseeable before the critical date, contending the investment was engineered to secure treaty protection.
probes.rationale: China-regime shape with a jurisdiction fight, never says patent/trademark. Ring 1 dense (clinical trial data + data exclusivity + covered investment + regulatory data protection + unfair commercial use + TRIPS 39 ~= 34) intersects Ring 3 (definition of investor + treaty shopping + reasonably foreseeable + critical date + treaty protection ~= 32). Two rings -> HIGH.

probes.text: The national medicines agency announced updated guidance on the disclosure of clinical trial data, aligning its transparency register with international norms. Under the new policy, summary results and portions of the trial dossier will be published after marketing approval, while genuinely commercially confidential trade secret material may be redacted on request. Industry groups welcomed the clarity but warned that over-broad disclosure of proprietary data could chill investment in research. The agency said the reform balances public-health transparency against legitimate commercial confidentiality and takes effect next year. No litigation, arbitration, or treaty dispute is associated with the announcement.
probes.rationale: Pure pharmaceutical regulatory NEWS with NO ISDS nexus: no claimant, no tribunal, no treaty claim. Yet it carries 'clinical trial data' and 'trade secret'. Must stay LOW. Critically, it lands the SAME Ring 1 subtotal (~17) as E2/E4 -> the instrument cannot lexically distinguish on-theme claims from off-theme news, because the discriminating signal (arbitration/treaty/claimant) lives in no ring.

probes.text: A commercial court has ruled in a trade secret misappropriation suit between two biotech firms. The claimant alleged a former employee copied confidential clinical trial data and proprietary manufacturing processes before joining the defendant. The court found misappropriation and awarded damages and an injunction. The dispute is a private commercial matter under national trade-secret law; no state measure, treaty, or investor-state arbitration is involved. The defendant has indicated it will appeal to the court of appeal. Both firms are domestically incorporated and the underlying events occurred entirely within a single jurisdiction. Commentators note that the case turns on ordinary employment and confidentiality obligations rather than any public act of the state, and that no host-state regulator, ministry, or arbitral tribunal features in it at all. The remaining questions concern the quantum of damages and the scope of the injunction; there is no cross-border or foreign-investor dimension of any kind.
probes.rationale: Trade-secret misappropriation in DOMESTIC court only, no ISDS. Carries 'trade secret' + 'clinical trial data' (Ring 1 ~17) but deliberately avoids the exact Ring 2 phrases 'domestic court' and 'Supreme Court' (uses 'commercial court' / 'court of appeal'). Must stay LOW. See report red-team: swapping in 'domestic court'/'Supreme Court' flips this to a FALSE POSITIVE (Ring 2 present), a documented brittleness.

probes.text: A mining company initiated arbitration after the host state revoked its copper mineral concession by executive decree. The claim alleges direct expropriation of the concession and seeks compensation for the lost operation, arguing that the decree stripped it of a long-held extraction right without adequate compensation. The respondent state maintains that the revocation followed environmental non-compliance findings and was a lawful exercise of regulatory power. There is no pharmaceutical, data-protection, or judicial-conduct dimension to the dispute, and no intellectual property of any kind is asserted; it is a straightforward mineral concession expropriation of exactly the kind the watcher expressly excludes as off-theme. The tribunal's task is confined to valuation and the lawfulness of the decree.
probes.rationale: Off-theme control that trips a negative_signal ('mineral concession'). Confirms the negative-signal machinery still forces LOW with no ring rescue. Must stay LOW under both current and proposed weights.

probes.text: A construction conglomerate brings a treaty claim after the host state terminated its toll-road concession. The investor alleges the termination and subsequent measures were an indirect expropriation and unfair treatment, and disputes the state's jurisdictional objection on the definition of investor. The dispute is a pure infrastructure and contract matter, unrelated to pharmaceuticals, data rights, or brands, and no court judgment is challenged. The claim rests on the economics of the concession agreement and the state's alleged failure to honour negotiated tariff guarantees over the operating period. Engineering, project-financing, and force-majeure questions dominate the pleadings on both sides. Nothing in the record touches proprietary research, confidential submissions, or any exclusive commercial right; the tribunal is asked only to value the terminated concession and to rule on the standing objection the respondent has raised.
probes.rationale: Investment dispute with NO intellectual property of any kind, light jurisdiction pleading ('definition of investor' only, sub-floor). Must stay LOW. Guards against Ring 3 alone dragging a non-IP infrastructure case over the line; also checks that the proposed Ring 1 near-miss additions do not accidentally fire on 'data rights'/'brands'.

probes.text: Eli Lilly-type claim. The pharmaceutical claimant challenges the invalidation of its drug patents by domestic courts applying the promise utility doctrine and a heightened utility requirement. It frames the patents as a covered investment and the judicial measure as a denial of justice breaching the minimum standard of treatment, alleging manifest arbitrariness in the dramatic change in the utility requirement worked by the courts. The claimant contends the invalidation reversed decades of settled patent-office practice and defeated the legitimate expectations on which its research investment was built. It seeks compensation for the destruction of its patent portfolio, characterising the domestic court rulings throughout as a judicial measure that was arbitrary or discriminatory and that no honest tribunal applying the prior standard could have reached, and it invokes the fair-and-equitable-treatment guarantee of the applicable treaty.
probes.rationale: Seed-shaped control (Eli Lilly v. Canada). Ring 1 (promise utility doctrine + utility requirement + covered investment) intersects Ring 2 (denial of justice + judicial measure + domestic court + minimum standard of treatment + manifest arbitrariness). Must remain HIGH under current AND proposed weights, or the reweight has broken the seed.

probes.text: Bridgestone / Philip Morris-type claim. A brand owner asserts its trademark and the licenses that constitute its investment as a covered investment, and challenges a Supreme Court manifestly unjust judgment as a denial of justice. The respondent pleads abuse of process, treaty shopping, and corporate restructuring through a shell subsidiary to gain treaty protection, disputing the standing of licensor vs licensee to bring the claim. The tribunal must first resolve whether the restructuring was a legitimate business decision or an abusive tactic undertaken once the dispute was reasonably foreseeable, and only then reach the merits of the denial-of-justice claim against the apex court's ruling. The claimant maintains that its brand and licensing arrangements were long-standing operating assets, not a device manufactured to secure treaty protection, and that the impugned judgment shocks a sense of judicial propriety.
probes.rationale: Seed-shaped control (Bridgestone v. Panama / Philip Morris v. Australia). Three rings: Ring 1 (trademark + licenses that constitute its investment + covered investment + licensor/licensee), Ring 2 (Supreme Court + manifestly unjust judgment + denial of justice), Ring 3 (abuse of process + treaty shopping + corporate restructuring + shell subsidiary + treaty protection). Must remain HIGH under current AND proposed weights.
